title: Vexa station report v1 — the inbound half of the contract
description:
What a customer's estate is permitted to send back to Vexa, stated as a closed schema rather than a promise. The payload is ONE commented YAML file the operator reads top to bottom before it leaves; this schema is that file's whole permitted field set, and the submit tool validates the document itself rather than a summary assembled beside it. Every object in this document sets additionalProperties:false, so the permitted field set is the WHOLE field set: there is no place to put a transcript, a meeting title, a participant, a mail body, a log line or a free-text note, and a payload that carries one fails validation before it is sent rather than being caught in review afterwards. That is the design claim — not that we would not read content, but that the format cannot carry it.

Three properties beyond the field list, all enforced by the submit tool (kit/validate/vexa_validate.py --submit) and all writable as contract clauses (report_scope in the verify policy):
  * TRIGGER — an explicit operator command, never a timer, a hook, or a running process. Nothing in the delivered software originates a report.
  * DESTINATION — the channel host the estate already pulls from, and only that host. No new firewall rule, no second vendor endpoint, no third party.
  * PAYLOAD — ONE FILE, `station-report.yaml`, whose section roles are enumerated in the contract (report_scope.allowed_sections). A report carrying a section outside those roles is refused locally, before a byte moves.

The outbound half of the same contract is delivery_scope: what a release may do inside the customer's cluster. The two are deliberately symmetric — a subscription is a pair of bounded promises, and each is a file the customer can read and tighten.

No standards body has defined this document; nobody has standardised what telemetry may leave a perimeter. The vocabulary is OpenTelemetry-shaped where a match exists and is OURS where none does, which is stated rather than dressed up.

allOf.$comment: THE TELEMETRY LADDER, ENFORCED BY THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN BY TWO TOOLS AGREEING. The station packager and our ingest both validate against this file, so the rung a payload occupies is decided in ONE place. A tool-side check would be two implementations of one rule, which is the shape every silent divergence in this system has taken.

bundle_kind.description: Which of the two shapes this bundle is, because they carry different evidence and refusing one for lacking the other's files was a real defect. `install` is the operator's validation run — preflight, install, smoke — and carries all six file roles. `telemetry` is a ladder submission from the station itself: no phase ran, so there is no preflight or smoke receipt to carry, and demanding one would mean either refusing every T2 bundle or manufacturing an empty receipt. Absent means `install`, which is what every bundle written before the ladder existed was.

tier.description:
The telemetry-ladder rung this payload occupies, and never higher than the rung the station's own contract declares in report_scope.tier. T0 silent (nothing leaves; a T0 station does not submit at all) · T1 receipts (install and validation verdicts, per release) · T2 health (aggregate counters, no identities, no content) · T3 usage (activated-user and volume counts, pseudonymous). T4 — scrubbed diagnostics — has NO value here on purpose: it is never automatic and never travels this path. It is exported locally by the customer's own admin, read by them, and handed over out of band per incident. A schema that could express T4 would be a schema that could carry one automatically.

CONTENT IS NOT ON THE LADDER AT ANY TIER. There is no rung at which a transcript, a meeting title, a participant or a log line becomes permitted, which is why additionalProperties is false on every object below rather than only on the ones a reviewer would think to check.

Absent means tier 1: every payload written before the ladder existed is a release receipt, and reading it as anything else would either invent data it does not have or refuse evidence that is already in the ledger.

station.description: The station's name — the customer's own label for this install. Also the path segment it may push to on the channel, and the only identifier in the document.

kit.description: Which revision of OUR software produced this. Ours, not theirs.

namespaces.description: Names of namespaces, not their contents.

contract.description: WHICH promise this run was judged against — id and hash, never the clauses.

phases.description: VERDICTS AND EXIT CODES ONLY. The receipt fields carry a FILENAME, never the file's text — the bytes travel as bundle members the operator can open, so nothing here is a channel for prose.

redaction.description: Counts, and the names of files that leaked — never a leaked value, and never a redacted one.

release.description: T1 — WHAT IS RUNNING HERE, AND UNDER WHAT VERDICT. The rung that buys support entitlement, because it is the rung at which we can answer 'which bytes are they on?' without asking. Identifiers and digests only: an app name, a pin, an entry position, sync and health words from Argo, and the PreSync verifier's verdict. Nothing in this object can hold a workload's data — there is no field for it.

app.description: The Argo CD Application name. Their label for the subscription, not ours.

pin.description: The position the Application follows — an exact version on production, `*` on staging.

entry_seq.description: Channel entry sequence the pin resolves to. The channel's own ordering, echoed back so a divergence between what we promoted and what they follow is visible from one side.

verifier.description: The PreSync gate's own verdict on this sync. ELIGIBLE means every check the subscriber's contract asked for passed; ABSENT means the gate did not run, which is a finding rather than a pass.

images.description: Digests only. A repository name and a sha256 — the same pair the entry already names, echoed from what is actually running, which is the only way a drift between the two is detectable at all.

health.description:
T2 — AGGREGATE COUNTERS. Integers and ratios over the workloads the subscription manages. NO IDENTITIES, NO CONTENT, NO LOGS: there is no field here that can hold a pod's output, an error message, a user, a meeting or a hostname. The rung buys us seeing a degradation before they file a ticket, and it buys them a vendor who already knows. Cadence is theirs — daily by default, weekly if they say so.

Workload NAMES appear (a Deployment is called what the chart called it, and a restart count without one says nothing actionable). Those names are OUR chart's, not their data.

window_hours.description: How much time the counters cover. A restart count with no window is not a number.

restarts.description: Summed container restarts across the Deployment's pods.

last_success_age_seconds.description: Null means it has never succeeded, which is different from zero and must not be rendered as fresh.

nodes.description: Capacity as counts and percentages. Node NAMES are not here — they are the customer's infrastructure and say nothing we need.

pods.description: Phase counts. Which pods, and why, is a T4 question.

absent.description: Counters this run could NOT collect, each with a reason — RBAC it does not hold, a metrics API the cluster does not serve. Absent-over-faked: a missing counter is reported missing rather than defaulted to zero, because zero is a claim.

usage.description:
T3 — VOLUME AND ACTIVATION AGGREGATES, pseudonymous. Counts of activated users, meetings, minutes and per-model token consumption. The rung that buys benchmarks against the fleet, tuned defaults and capacity planning.

SHIPPED AS AN INTERFACE WITH NO IMPLEMENTATION, on purpose. Nothing in this repository can produce these numbers today: the product's usage surface is not exposed to a station-side collector, and inventing plausible ones would put fabricated data into a customer's ledger under a signature. So the collector reports `absent` with a reason, and a T3 station gets an honest empty rung until the exporter exists. ABSENT OVER FAKED.

When it does exist: still no identities. `activated_users` is a COUNT. There is no field for a user, a meeting title, a participant or a transcript, and there is no rung at which one appears.

tokens_by_model.description: Model identifier -> token count. The only open-keyed object in this schema, and its keys are constrained to model-name shape and its values to integers, so it cannot become a place to put a string.

profile.description: The provider profile this run used, verbatim. Substrate facts — provider, Kubernetes version, scope, storage class, PSA mode, mirror host — and never credentials.

values.description: The operator's values file, structurally intact, with every secret-looking value replaced by REDACTED. The SHAPE is the contribution; the values are not.

contract_document.description: The contract this run was judged against, verbatim, beside its id and sha256 in `contract`. The report states the policy it was produced under rather than referring to one.

install_log.description: The install log, present only when --install ran. A console, so the packager keeps its tail and records the trim in sections[].

smoke_console.description: The smoke run's console, tail-trimmed. Kept because a run that dies before writing its receipt leaves nothing else, and evidence of a crash is still evidence.

absent.description: Sections this run could NOT produce, each with a reason. Absent over empty: a blank receipt because nothing ran and a blank receipt because a phase produced nothing look identical, and only one of them is fine.

refuses.description: What the tool that wrote this refuses to do, in its own words, so a reader of the document does not have to read the source to find out. Prose, and bounded: it is a list of the tool's own claims, not a channel.

sections.description: THE MANIFEST — every verbatim section above with the sha256 of its text. What used to be files[] over archive members, now over sections of one document: what travelled, and provably which bytes. Digests are over the normalised text (LF, no trailing whitespace, one final newline), so what is hashed is what is read.

source_lines.description: How many lines the section had before trimming, when it was trimmed. Present only then, and the trim is never silent.

section.description: ONE VERBATIM DOCUMENT, carried whole. These are the members the station bundle used to carry as files in a tarball; folding them into the report did not widen what may travel, it enumerated it — the seven names below are the whole set, additionalProperties is still false, and there is no eighth. The cap is not a budget, it is the claim that somebody read this before sending it: a section larger than a quarter of a megabyte is a dump.
